_about: Prices and payment links for /rain-print. Products: digital (the 12 x 18 print files, emailed), print12x18 (12 x 18 print, unframed, shipped rolled in a tube), framed12x18 (12 x 18 print in a black frame with an acrylic front, ready to hang); Sig prints, frames and ships them himself. The page reads this file; change a price here and the page follows. payment_links: paste a Stripe Payment Link (https://buy.stripe.com/...) per product. While a link is null, that button opens the order request form instead. The page adds client_reference_id=<design code> to the link, so each Stripe payment carries the design; open https://agsist.com/rain-print?d=<code> to see it. A gift order's code starts with GIFT- (this year's print: make it after January 1, once the December numbers are in); ?d= opens it with or without that prefix. Gift text (this year's print, ordered now and delivered in January): {year} becomes the current year and {next} the year after, on the page and the printed gift card. Say January, not a date: the print waits on NOAA's December numbers. Christmas cutoffs (print_christmas_cutoff, framed_christmas_cutoff, YYYY-MM-DD) are the last day an order still arrives by Dec 24 under the promise on the page: proof within proof_business_days, the buyer OKs it within approve_business_days, it ships within ship_business_days after that, and the carrier takes transit_business_days per product (weekends and holidays skipped). Change any of those numbers and set the two cutoffs to what RainPrint.christmasCutoff() gives; the test fails until they agree. From October 1 to the cutoff the print and framed cards say "Order by <date> for Christmas delivery."; after it, through Dec 25, they say new orders ship after Christmas. Next year: move holidays and the cutoffs to that year. This year's gift prints ship in January and show no cutoff. For businesses (the quote form under the prices, 10 to 500 prints; the worker refuses fewer than 10): business_cutoff (YYYY-MM-DD or null): when set, the section says "For Christmas, send your list by <Mon D>." through that date; after it, or while null, nothing about a date. business_note (null or one sentence): shown as written under the section; null shows nothing. business_tiers [{min, pct}]: an order of at least min prints gets pct percent off the per-print price of every product (digital, print12x18, framed12x18); the first tier's min should stay 10. business_shipping {print12x18, framed12x18, digital}: shipping in dollars per print on a business order, US addresses only. Shipped one to each customer, it is charged in full. business_shipping_one_address_tiers [{min, pct}]: pct percent off that shipping per print when the whole order goes to one address. The page builds its table (rows from business_tiers; price per print, then shipping per print to one address and to each customer) and the form's quote line from these and the prices above, rounded to the cent. business_tiers empty or missing: no table and no discount wording. business_shipping null or missing: "Shipping is quoted with your order." and no shipping columns. Consumer orders (the three cards above, shipping included) never use these.
ships_within: Prints and framed prints ship within 7 business days after you approve the proof. US addresses only for now.
gift_delivery: Sig makes the print once the station's December numbers are in, and it goes out in January {next}. You get a proof first, as with every order.
gift_card_title: Your {year} Rain Print is coming in January
gift_card_note: The finished print shows every day of rain from January 1 to December 31, {year}.
_promote: Seasonal promo, OFF by default. promote:true shows one line, "A year of your farm's rain, as a gift. Order framed by <framed_christmas_cutoff>.", linking /rain-print, on the homepage (under the briefing teaser) and /cash-bids (under the bids), only while today in America/Chicago is between promote_from and promote_until inclusive (components/rain-print-promo.js). briefing_line: null for none, or one sentence; with promote on and in the window it shows once near the end of /daily and of the daily email (scripts/brief_email.py rain_print_line).
